display.title: Episode 148: The Lost Letter, Chapter 3 (Shofar Gadol Contest Winners)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi announces the winners of the Shofar Gadol drawing contest, and the story ends: ten years late, Reb Leibel delivers the Baal Shem Tov's letter and learns what it says.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi opens with the grand finale of the Shofar Gadol contest, working up from the smallest entry, a few inches long, through family projects of nine and seventeen feet, to the winner: a drawing more than forty-eight feet long. Every entrant gets a gift, and the winners will be invited to say the Shema in the studio. The Hakochainik march is sung to 'Teka b'Shofar Gadol.' After a recap, a boy who loves signing up his friends for Tzivos Hashem leads the Shema, and the week's program is dedicated in memory of a sponsoring family's father. The story concludes: Reb Leibel, now poor and shabby, travels to deliver the Baal Shem Tov's letter to Reb Sholom, a wealthy former student. The guard will not let him in until Reb Sholom, hearing who wrote the letter, agrees to see him. Recognizing his teacher's seal, Reb Sholom reads it in tears: the Baal Shem Tov foresaw that Reb Leibel would pay for refusing a brachah and asked Reb Sholom to set him back on his feet. The letter is dated that very day. The lesson: never underestimate a brachah, especially from a tzaddik.
display.lesson: Never think you have no need of a brachah; a blessing, especially from a tzaddik, brings Hashem's goodness.
